review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for missing simp attributes, competing rules and unwanted unfolding. The file contains no `@[simp]` attribute at all. For the `LoewnerLocalized`/`FiniteTilt` parts, the companion lemmas (`clampIm_eq`, the `LoewnerField` `position_initial`, `logDerivative_initial`) come from other files, so their simp status is outside this file. I put most of the weight on the `BoundaryFunctional` section (lines 932–1249), which this file defines. Downstream it is used through `open BoundaryFunctional` in SwallowingLaws.lean and BoundaryDiffusion.lean. I checked the actual uses there: `simp only [... logDerivative_initial ... position_initial ...]`, three uses of `simp [position_im_zero]`, and `change BoundaryCutoff.clamp 1 ε _ = _` / `change 2/clampRe ε _ = _` used to see through the wrappers. I also read `BoundaryCutoff.clamp`, `BoundaryCutoff.velocity` and `BoundaryCutoff.clamp_eq` in SobolevMeans.lean, and the comparable `clampIm_eq` in StoppedIto.lean.

I found no rewrite cycles and no wrongly oriented rules. The `Swallowing` defs (`radial`, `radialX`, …) are unfolded on purpose with `unfold`/`dsimp` inside derivative proofs, so I did not flag them.

Limitations: I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed attributes or lemmas compile or that existing `simp` calls still close their goals. For example, a `simp only` list that already names a lemma would just become redundant. There is also a risk of name clashes: `BoundaryDiffusion.lean` reopens the `BoundaryFunctional` namespace (line 573), so any new names (`clampRe_eq`, `velocity_eq`) need to be checked against what it defines there. I did not read that section.

findings.excerpt:
lemma position_initial {ε T : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (U : C(I, ℝ)) (z : ℂ) : position hε hT U z 0 = z := by
findings.problem: The initial-value lemmas `solution_initial` (l.1060), `logDerivative_initial` (l.1153) and `position_initial` (l.1170) state the obvious normal forms: `position hε hT U z 0` should become `z` and `logDerivative hε hT U z 0` should become `0`. They have no hypotheses beyond the proof arguments, which unify, and each right-hand side is strictly smaller than its left-hand side. They are still not simp lemmas, so every caller has to list them by hand next to the usual arithmetic cleanup lemmas (`mul_zero`, `Real.exp_zero`, `sub_zero`). This happens in the file itself (`rw [solution_initial]; simp` in position_im_zero) and downstream.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `solution_initial`, `logDerivative_initial` and `position_initial` as `@[simp]`. The orientation is already correct (complex term to atom, cannot loop). Callers such as `simp only [field,factor,logDerivative_initial,mul_zero,Real.exp_zero,position_initial,...]` can then use plain `simp`/`simp [field, factor]`.
findings.benefit: Expressions evaluated at time 0 then simplify automatically to their canonical values, so downstream simp sets get shorter and easier to maintain. This matters because the same evaluation at time 0 appears in several files.

evidence.excerpt: (U : C(I, ℝ)) (z : ℂ) : logDerivative hε hT U z 0 = 0 := by

findings.excerpt:
lemma position_im_zero {ε T : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (U : C(I, ℝ)) (x t : ℝ) : (position hε hT U (x:ℂ) t).im = 0 := by
findings.problem: `(position hε hT U (↑x) t).im` always equals `0` with no side conditions: a flow that starts on the real line stays real. Every downstream use passes the lemma to `simp` by hand to prove `position … = ↑(position …).re`. That is three identical `apply Complex.ext <;> simp [position_im_zero]` blocks across two files. The left-hand side is a projection of a specific term and the right-hand side is the literal `0`, so the rule terminates and does not overlap with any rule I found.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the lemma `@[simp]`. Optionally also add `@[simp] lemma ofReal_re_position : ((position hε hT U (x:ℂ) t).re : ℂ) = position hε hT U (x:ℂ) t`, proved by `Complex.ext` with `position_im_zero`. The repeated `hz` helper could then be dropped or proved by plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: `simp` then knows the real-line invariant without being told, which removes the repeated hand-written `simp [position_im_zero]` blocks and makes the gap and real-part computations downstream shorter.

evidence.excerpt:
have hz : position hε hT U (x:ℂ) t = ((position hε hT U (x:ℂ) t).re:ℂ) := by
    apply Complex.ext <;> simp [position_im_zero]

findings.excerpt:
def clampRe (ε : ℝ) (w : ℂ) : ℂ := BoundaryCutoff.clamp 1 ε w

def velocity (ε u : ℝ) (w : ℂ) : ℂ := BoundaryCutoff.velocity 1 ε u w
findings.problem: These wrapper definitions come with no equation lemmas. There is no `clampRe_eq` (the clamp does nothing once `ε ≤ w.re`), unlike the analogous `clampIm_eq` that this file uses heavily. There is also no lemma saying `velocity ε u w = 2 / clampRe ε (w - u)`. As a result, callers either unfold two layers of definitions with simp (`simp [velocity,BoundaryCutoff.velocity]`, l.973) or use `change` to expose `BoundaryCutoff.clamp 1 ε _` / `2/clampRe ε _` before rewriting with `BoundaryCutoff.clamp_eq (by norm_num : |(1:ℝ)|=1)`. Both spill the σ = 1 implementation detail into downstream proofs.
findings.proposed_change: Add `lemma clampRe_eq {ε : ℝ} {w : ℂ} (hw : ε ≤ w.re) : clampRe ε w = w := BoundaryCutoff.clamp_eq (by norm_num) (by simpa using hw)`. This is the conditional counterpart of `clampIm_eq` and is usable in `simp [clampRe_eq h]`. Also add `lemma velocity_eq (ε u : ℝ) (w : ℂ) : velocity ε u w = 2 / clampRe ε (w - (u:ℂ)) := rfl`. Rewrite `norm_velocity_driver_sub_le`'s `he` with `simp [velocity_eq]`, and replace the downstream `change BoundaryCutoff.clamp 1 ε _ = _; rw [BoundaryCutoff.clamp_eq …]` with `rw [clampRe_eq …]`.
findings.benefit: Users get rewrite rules stated in terms of the file's own vocabulary, so proofs no longer depend on how `BoundaryCutoff` is parameterised. The `change` steps, which break easily, go away. The boundary API also ends up matching the `clampIm_eq` interface that the interior version already provides.

evidence.excerpt: lemma clampIm_eq {ε : ℝ} {w : ℂ} (hw : ε ≤ w.im) : clampIm ε w = w := by
